transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

...Hi. Um, well... I guess I'm here because things have been difficult at work lately. I've been... stepping back from things. Avoiding presentations, mostly. And clients. 

It's... it's hard to talk about, but... it's my face. I just can't stop seeing this... this droop around my mouth. And my jaw, it's just so uneven. Every photo, every reflection I walk past... it's all I see. People tell me I look fine, but... I know what I see. It's so obvious to me. So I just... try to stay out of sight.
How long have you been feeling this way about the appearance of your face, and does it happen every time you see your reflection?

I'm not exactly sure when it started. Just... a while, I guess. 

And... yeah. Every time. It's... it's always there when I look.
When you notice the unevenness in your face, do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors repeatedly, touching your face, or trying to fix it in your mind?

Yes... I suppose I do. Especially before work, or if I have to see family. I can spend... hours, just checking the bathroom mirror. Taking pictures on my phone from different angles to see how bad it is. 

I try to fix it, or... hide it. Redoing my makeup over and over, or adjusting my scarf. I'll ask my husband if my face looks lopsided. And... I guess I also spend a lot of time scrolling through photos of other women online. Just comparing. Seeing how bad mine looks beside theirs. 

It's... yeah. I do that.
Does this concern about your face cause you a lot of distress, or has it affected your ability to do normal things like work or spend time with family?

...Yeah. It does. 

Um... I actually cancelled a major client presentation recently. Right at the last minute. I just... I couldn't face being seen. And I've been missing out on some networking events for awards, too, because of it. 

So... my project deadlines are kind of falling apart right now. And... family gatherings are, too. I just... it's hard.
